We report the case of a patient presenting with Tetralogy of Fallots and dental anomalies without any ocular features.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the genotype/phenotype relationship in patients carrying PITx2 deletions.
the description of a new patient with a 4q25 micro-deletion, the first reported with a TOF and no ocular malformation.
the identification of the genotype-phenotype relationship in patients carrying 4p16.3 and 4q25 micro-deletions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PITX2 haplodeficiency is not sufficient to cause ocular malformations in all patients, and that the phenotype of PITX2 haploid patients may vary from a mild phenotype to an ARS phenotype.
TOF and PIT2 haploinsufficientity are not associated.
TOF is a rare extra-ocular manifestation in PITX2 haplodeficient patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PITX2 deletion is not a major cause of TOF, but may be one of several genetic factors that contribute to this congenital cardiac defect.
the deletion of PITX 2 is not always associated with ocular malformation, and that PITX2 could be involved in the pathogenesis of TOF.
the 4q deletion syndrome is a heterogeneous disorder with variable expressivity, even within the same family.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a PITX2 microdeletion should be considered in patients with TOF and dental abnormalities.
the ocular malformations associated with PITX2 haplodeficiency are not mandatory.
PITX2 haplosufficiency is not necessarily responsible for ARA and other ocular defects.
